exam.title: MuleSoft Certified Developer – Level 1 (practice)
exam.note: Original practice questions written for DWCode. They are not taken from the real exam.

questions.prompt: In API-led connectivity, which layer unlocks data from core systems of record?
questions.explanation: System APIs expose systems of record; Process APIs orchestrate them; Experience APIs shape data for a channel.

questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of a Center for Enablement (C4E)?
options: To centralise every integration build in one team
To drive reuse and self-service of integration assets across teams
To replace API governance with code reviews
questions.explanation: A C4E enables lines of business to build and reuse assets themselves, rather than funnelling everything through one central team.

questions.prompt: What is Anypoint Exchange used for?
options: Discovering and sharing reusable assets such as API specs, connectors and templates
questions.explanation: Exchange is the catalog of reusable assets; Runtime Manager deploys and API Manager applies policies.

questions.prompt: In a RAML spec, what does `/{orderId}` nested under `/orders` declare?
options: A nested resource with a URI parameter named orderId
questions.explanation: Curly braces in a resource path declare a URI parameter.

questions.prompt: Which HTTP method is defined as idempotent?
questions.explanation: Repeating a PUT leaves the resource in the same state; POST and PATCH are not guaranteed to be idempotent.

questions.prompt: What does the mocking service let you do with an API spec in Design Center?
options: Let consumers try the API before it is implemented
questions.explanation: The mocking service returns example responses from the spec, so consumers can give feedback early.

questions.prompt: What does a Mule 4 event contain?
options: A message (payload and attributes) and variables
questions.explanation: A Mule event is a message (payload plus attributes) and the event's variables.

questions.prompt: In a flow started by an HTTP Listener, which expression reads the query parameter `name`?
questions.explanation: Request metadata from the HTTP Listener — query parameters, URI parameters, headers — is in `attributes`.

questions.prompt: When a flow calls another flow through a Flow Reference, what happens to its variables?
options: They are copied, and changes are discarded
They are only visible if marked global
They are cleared before the call
The referenced flow sees them, and its changes are visible after it returns
questions.explanation: Flow Reference passes the same event, variables included, to the referenced flow and back.

questions.prompt: How does a subflow differ from a flow?
options: It has no event source and no error handling of its own
It must live in its own file
questions.explanation: A subflow is a reusable block executed inline by Flow Reference; it has no source and inherits the caller's error handling.

questions.prompt: Where do you define a configuration (such as an HTTP Listener config) reused by several flows?
questions.explanation: Global elements hold shared configurations referenced by name from any flow in the application.

questions.prompt: Which syntax reads a property such as `http.port` from a properties file in a configuration?
questions.explanation: Property placeholders use `${...}`; `#[...]` is a DataWeave expression.

questions.prompt: What does APIkit generate from a RAML or OAS specification?
options: A router plus a flow for each resource and method, with error handlers
questions.explanation: APIkit scaffolds a main flow with the APIkit Router, one flow per resource/method, and error handling.

questions.prompt: An APIkit-based API receives a request for a resource that is not in its spec. Which error does the router raise?
questions.explanation: The APIkit Router raises APIKIT:NOT_FOUND, which the scaffolded handler maps to 404.

questions.prompt: What does the APIkit Router check before routing a request?
options: That the request matches the spec (resource, method, parameters, body)
That the payload is under 1 MB
That the client has a valid OAuth token
questions.explanation: The router validates requests against the spec; authentication is the job of policies.

questions.prompt: How does the Choice router pick a route?
options: It runs the first route whose condition is true, else the default route
It runs every route whose condition is true
It picks a route at random
questions.explanation: Choice evaluates conditions in order and runs only the first match, falling back to the default.

questions.prompt: What is the output of a Scatter-Gather?
options: The payload of the fastest route
An object keyed by route index, holding each route's result message
questions.explanation: Scatter-Gather runs routes concurrently and aggregates each route's resulting Mule message into one object keyed by route.

questions.prompt: What does the First Successful router do?
options: Runs all routes and keeps the first result
Retries the same route until it succeeds
Tries its routes in order until one completes without an error
Runs routes in parallel and cancels the slow ones
questions.explanation: First Successful moves to the next route only when the current one fails.

questions.prompt: An error is handled by On Error Continue. What does the caller of the flow see?
options: A successful result: the handler's output
questions.explanation: On Error Continue handles the error and completes the flow successfully; On Error Propagate rethrows it to the caller.

questions.prompt: What is the format of a Mule error type?
questions.explanation: Error types are namespaced identifiers such as HTTP:NOT_FOUND or MULE:EXPRESSION.

questions.prompt: What does a Try scope let you do?
options: Roll back a database transaction by default
Handle errors for a group of processors inside a flow
questions.explanation: Try wraps processors with its own error handling, so errors can be handled without ending the flow.

questions.prompt: What does `["a", "b", "c"] map $$` return?
questions.explanation: `$$` is the index inside `map`.

questions.prompt: Which header directive makes a script produce JSON?
questions.explanation: `output` sets the format of the script's result; `input` declares how an input is read.

questions.prompt: What does `{a: 1} ++ {b: 2}` return?
questions.explanation: `++` concatenates objects.

questions.prompt: What does `sizeOf("hello")` return?
questions.explanation: `sizeOf` counts characters in a string.

questions.prompt: `payload` is `[{"id": 1, "active": true}, {"id": 2, "active": false}]`. What does `payload filter $.active` return?
questions.explanation: `filter` keeps items whose condition is true; `$.active` is that condition.

questions.prompt: What does `do { fun double(n) = n * 2 --- double(4) }` return?
questions.explanation: `do` scopes a local function declaration; calling it returns 8.

questions.prompt: What does `upper("mule")` return?
questions.explanation: `upper` converts a string to upper case.

questions.prompt: What does a Database Select operation return?
options: The matching rows, each as a key–value map of column to value
questions.explanation: Select returns the result rows as a list of records keyed by column name.

questions.prompt: How does the Scheduler component start a flow?
options: On a fixed frequency or a cron expression
questions.explanation: The Scheduler is an event source that triggers a flow on a schedule.

questions.prompt: Where should credentials such as a database password be kept in a Mule application?
options: In secure (encrypted) properties, referenced by placeholder
questions.explanation: Secure properties keep secrets encrypted and out of source; the configuration references them with a placeholder.

questions.prompt: What are the phases of a batch job?
options: Load and dispatch, process, on complete
questions.explanation: A batch job loads and dispatches records into a queue, processes them through steps, then runs On Complete.

questions.prompt: What is a Batch Aggregator for?
options: Grouping records so a step can process them in bulk
questions.explanation: An aggregator collects records into groups, for example for a bulk insert.

questions.prompt: What does the Anypoint Studio debugger let you do?
options: Pause at breakpoints and inspect the Mule event
questions.explanation: The debugger stops at breakpoints on processors so you can inspect payload, attributes and variables.

questions.prompt: Where do you read the logs of an application deployed to CloudHub?
options: In Runtime Manager, on the application's logs page
questions.explanation: Runtime Manager shows deployment and application logs.

questions.prompt: What does API Manager let you do with an API instance?
options: Apply and configure policies, and manage client access
questions.explanation: API Manager governs a running API: policies, SLA tiers and client applications.

questions.prompt: What does API Autodiscovery do?
options: Finds APIs on the public internet
Pairs a deployed application with its API Manager instance so policies apply
questions.explanation: Autodiscovery links the running app to the API instance so API Manager can enforce its policies.

questions.prompt: What does the Client ID Enforcement policy require from a caller?
options: A source IP on an allow list
A client_id and client_secret of an approved client application
questions.explanation: Client ID Enforcement checks the credentials of a client application registered for the API.
